quote: 10. Stochastic Ordering. A crucial technique in reliability and finance for evaluating the relative performance of the models is stochastic ordering. Let X and Y be two random variables with pdf, cdf, and reliability functions f(x), f(y), F(x), F(y), S(x) = 1 − F(x) and F(y). 1- Likelihood ratio order (X ≤ Y) if f(x;η,β)/f(x;η,β) decreases in x. 2- Stochastic order (X ≤ Y) if F(x;x;η,β) ≥ F(x;η,β) ∀ x. 3- Hazard rate order (X ≤ Y) if h(x;η,β) ≥ F(x;η,β) ∀ x. 4- Mean residual life order (X ≤ Y) if MRL(X) ≤ MRL(X) ∀ x. Prove that the mixture of Gompertz and gamma distribution complies with the ordering with the highest likelihood (the likelihood ratio ordering). Assume that X and Y are two independent Random variables with probability distribution function f(x; η, β) and f(x; ψ, δ). If η < ψ and β < δ, then Λ = f(x;η,β)/f(x;ψ,δ) = [η/(1+β) e^{ηx}e^{βe^{ηx}−1} + (η²β/2)x e^{−ηx}] / [ψ/(1+δ) e^{ψx}e^{δe^{ψx}−1} + (ψ²δ/2)x e^{−ψx}]. Therefore, log[Λ] = log(η(1+δ)/ψ(1+β)) + log(...) − log(...). Differentiating with respect to x, ∂log[Λ]/∂x = [...] Hence, [∂logΛ/∂x] < 0, if η < ψ, β < δ.
